current.text: LaMelo Ball was traded to Minnesota and Miles Bridges to Phoenix, so Charlotte's lead creation role is open.
Experts expect his usage to rise to about 29 or 30 percent, with more creation and more assists, though his efficiency may drop.
He could become a four-threes-a-game player in the new Charlotte setup.
Coby White is out with a calf injury and will probably miss the start of the season. Kon Knueppel is also hurt. Miller is the last healthy main player in Charlotte.
While White is out, expect high volume, big minutes and more playmaking early in the season. His shooting may suffer.
He had no shoulder restrictions heading into training camp.
He is a projected starter next to White, Knueppel, Reid and Diabaté.
Charlotte has no single primary creator. Ball handling is expected to be split among White, Knueppel and Miller.
Charlotte is leaning fully into floor spacing and plans to take a lot of threes.
Experts see him as a clear third-round pick in category leagues. They call an ADP in the mid-40s too late, and an ESPN ADP near 107 far too late. A top-30 season is possible.
In an auction mock draft he was one of Josh's targets, and Josh bought him for 26 USD.
Some improvement in his fourth season is expected but not guaranteed.
With a March 28 end, Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. It has 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte's two-game week starting March 1 should not change decisions about him.

durable.text: He had shoulder surgery after the 2025-26 season. He gets injured often.
His drives often stall, which leads to many mid-range shots. He finishes well at the rim but rarely gets there.
Threes are his standout category. He makes far more than the pool, and even more so for a forward.
He is not a strong FG% player. His FG% on high volume is weak for a forward.
His turnovers are high for a forward.
Lloyd values him more in category leagues than in ESPN points leagues.

note: Experts treat him as a third-round value with top-30 upside, which is above his Yahoo rank of 35 and well above ESPN's 9 USD value. A price between our league's 20 USD from last season and Yahoo's 26 USD value fits that view, and Josh paid 26 USD in a mock. He fits punt FG% and punt TO builds best: about 3.4 threes, strong FT% and points, but 43% FG on 16 to 18 shots and about 2.7 turnovers. Early on, check his Yahoo Q (Leg) status and the shoulder, and see whether the extra usage while Coby White is out drags his FG% and turnovers down further.
